newsitem.title: CROATIA: Austrians eye Croatian tourism investment -agency.
newsitem.headline: Austrians eye Croatian tourism investment -agency.

text.p: The Croatian subsidiary of Bank Austria and Austria Trend Hotels are inquiring into the possibility of investment in tourism on Croatia's southern coast, news agency Hina reported on Thursday.
It said representatives of investors visited several hotels and tourist complexes in Dubrovnik, dubbed the "Pearl of the Adriatic", to check on their state and earning potential.

"The Dubrovnik hotels, which reflect tradition combined with a rich cultural heritage, have exceptional chances of development," Kurt Cleindienst, director of Austria Trend Hotels, was quoted as saying.
Croatia has already borrowed abroad to repair part of the bombing devastation on hotels from the 1991 siege by the former Yugoslav army at the outset of the bloody Balkan conflict.
But hoping to cash in on the recovery of its once lucrative tourist trade, it has so far stopped short of offering seaside facilities for sale to foreign investors.

Although most hotels suffered no direct war damage, many require substantial investment into refurbishment as they were used to shelter refugees from embattled zones. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
